learningObjectives: Configure a Python application for deployment across environments.
Manage environment variables and application secrets safely.
Understand the stages involved in deploying a Python service to the cloud.

activities.title: Deployment Pipeline
activities.instruction: Arrange the major stages from application code to a running cloud service.

content.concept: Cloud deployment typically involves preparing the application, configuring its runtime, building or packaging it, deploying it, and verifying that the service is healthy.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

goal: 6. Run health checks and verify the deployment

activities.title: Environment Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the parts of a Python application's deployment environment.

content.concept: An application environment combines the runtime, dependencies, configuration, secrets, external services, and networking needed to run the application.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Provides the Python interpreter and runtime used by the service.
Libraries required by the application, commonly installed from a dependency file.
Non-secret configuration values that can vary between environments.
Sensitive values such as credentials and API keys that should be managed securely.
The persistent data service used by the application.
The network port on which the application accepts requests.
An endpoint or mechanism used to determine whether the deployed service is functioning.

content.concept: The same application code can run in different environments by supplying environment-specific configuration externally.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Read DATABASE_URL from an environment variable
Hard-code the production database URL in source code
Commit production API keys to Git
Use the development database credentials in every environment
config.answer: Read DATABASE_URL from an environment variable
